overview: Retrospective review of incident reports and the pharmacy intervention log for the three shortage episodes, estimating substitution-related error rates by episode.
population: All doses of the three substituted products dispensed during their shortage episodes, and all incident reports and intervention log entries in the same periods.
exposure: Dispensing of a substituted product during a shortage episode.
procedures: The resident searches incident report free text with pre-specified product and concentration terms, matches entries to episode dates and products, and reviews the intervention log for the same products. Up to 150 charts are reviewed to confirm classification. A second pharmacist classifies a random 20 percent independently.

outcomes.name: Substitution-related medication errors
outcomes.measure: Errors per 1,000 doses dispensed, by episode
outcomes.why: Comparable across episodes of different size.

outcomes.name: Error type and stage
outcomes.measure: Distribution of wrong dose, dilution, rate or product by prescribing, preparation or administration
outcomes.why: Shows where to intervene next time.

outcomes.name: Errors reaching the patient
outcomes.measure: Proportion of errors that reached the patient, with harm category

feasibility: Dispensing counts are available from the pharmacy system; 100 resident hours cover free-text search, log review and 150 charts.

biasFlags.label: Under-reporting in incident reports
biasFlags.note: Partly offset by the intervention log.

parsimony.simplestPath: Three episodes, two sources, one rate per episode.

theoreticalFramework: SEIPS 2.0 to classify where in the work system substitution errors arose.
summary: Retrospective two-source review with a work-system framework.
